key_insight: The paper shows that adversarial robustness in quantum machine learning can be formally certified from measurement outcomes using a fidelity-based lower bound, and tightened optimally with semidefinite programming when model details are known.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical path to trustworthy QML on NISQ hardware by linking theory, software verification, and real-device validation in one workflow.
method: Derive a fidelity-based robustness lower bound from output measurement distributions.
Compute the optimal robustness bound via semidefinite programming when full model information is available.
Package the framework into VeriQR for automated QML robustness verification and benchmarking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the first experimental benchmark of quantum adversarial robustness on a 20-qubit superconducting processor, supporting both formal and physical validation.
watch_item: The strongest certification results depend on model knowledge for SDP-based optimization, while hardware noise and measurement uncertainty may affect real-device robustness estimates.
paper_title: Verifying Adversarial Robustness in Quantum Machine Learning: from theory to physical validation via a software tool
